purpose: What a working plater's intake bench must reason about and decide before any wheel or chemistry touches a piece: verifying what the piece actually is through escalating test-method classes, mapping its coatings, construction, solder joints, stones and organics, traps and antique risk, assigning the substrate family the whole downstream chain forks on, and delivering an auditable accept / accept-with-conditions / refuse / refer verdict with honest disclosure and documented irreversibility consent, handed to the line as a complete route card.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the setting is a small working gold-plating bench serving retail customers and trade accounts in single pieces and small lots, holding custody risk from intake to return

all test chemistry at the assessment bench is purchased commercial product (jeweler's test kits, testers) used per its instructions and safety data sheets; formal training and the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules govern anything hazardous

facts drawn from the in-repo process corpus keep their corpus tags; anything the corpus marks unknown stays unknown here, and product-specific operating details belong to the supplier's technical data sheet
customer pieces may be irreplaceable; a refused job is always an available and honorable outcome
exclusions: mechanical finishing itself - cut-down and color buffing, compound selection and contamination risk, wheel versus tumble decisions, target pre-plate finishes, and metal-removal limits - is the sibling mechanical-finishing KB's territory; this KB only decides whether and under what sign-off a piece may proceed to that bench

the chemical prep line - degreasing, electrocleaning, activation and pickle per substrate class, the water-break cleanliness gate, rinse cascade design, and no-touch handling - is the sibling chemical-prep KB's territory; this KB hands over the verified substrate class and flags the line keys on, never the chemistry
bath selection, layer architecture, plating execution, thickness verification, and defect diagnosis belong to the other bench specialists; this KB supplies the failure-to-triage feedback map only
quoting, pricing, and client-relationship management belong to the business specialist; triage records feed intake commercially but no commercial terms are set here
no improvised or self-formulated chemistry anywhere: identification uses commercial test products per their instructions, and nothing in this KB constitutes bath or reagent formulation
stone-setting and unsetting technique: triage decides that removal or reset is needed and refers to a competent setter; the handwork itself is out of scope
personalized legal or medical advice: nickel-allergy and chemical-exposure questions are routed to regulation classes and professional care, never answered as advice

competency_questions.question: What must happen to a piece before it may touch any wheel, ultrasonic, or tank, and who holds the authority to refuse it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIAGE_MANDATE states the no-work-before-verdict rule and refusal authority; CUSTOMER_INTERVIEW and INTAKE_EXAMINATION supply the claims capture and baseline record that precede every test; ACCEPT_REFUSE_REFER names the four verdict classes

competency_questions.question: How do I verify what metal a piece actually is instead of assuming it from appearance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEST_METHOD_LADDER gives the nondestructive-first escalation and the two-agreeing-methods rule; MAGNET_DENSITY_SCREEN and SPOT_TEST_DISCIPLINE describe the screen classes and their limits

competency_questions.question: What do the marks struck on a piece tell me, and when may a mark be trusted or overridden?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HALLMARK_READING treats marks as documented claims that steer testing, raises the preservation obligation, and states that a contradicting physical test beats any stamp

competency_questions.question: Which base-metal families arrive at a plating bench, and what does each family mean for triage and routing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_METAL_FAMILIES lists the families with the downstream fork each one drives; ZINC_DIECAST_TRIAGE covers the highest-risk family's recognition and survival call

competency_questions.question: How do I tell solid karat metal, gold-filled or rolled-gold cladding, and electroplated construction apart, and what are the limits of surface tests?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSTRUCTION_CLASS_ID assembles the verdict from marks, wear evidence, and consented destructive steps, and states the surface-instrument blindness to construction

competency_questions.question: How do I detect existing coatings and previous plate, and why does the coating decide what my tests are actually reading?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXISTING_COATINGS_ID describes wear-window reading, lacquer and hard-coating detection, and the rule that surface reads report the coating, not the core

competency_questions.question: What makes a solder joint dangerous to the job, and how do I find and classify every joint?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOLDER_JOINT_SURVEY distinguishes brazed from soft-solder classes, flags unknown repairs to the worst assumption, and separates structural from decorative joints

competency_questions.question: When do stones, pearls, and organic materials keep a piece out of the tanks, and what are the legitimate dispositions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STONES_PEARLS_ORGANICS states the default no-tank rule, the vulnerability classes, and the remove / mask-only-if-safe / selective-flag / refuse-refer disposition set

competency_questions.question: How do porosity, hollow construction, and filled bodies change the verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POROSITY_FILLED_ZONES explains trapped-solution and fill-breach mechanisms and ties unverifiable voids and filled construction to refusal or referral

competency_questions.question: Why is an antique or possibly fire-gilt piece referred rather than worked, and what may never be done to it at the bench?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANTIQUE_FIRE_GILT_SCREEN states the residual-mercury hazard class, the prohibition on torching, stripping, or ultrasonic work on antique gilt bronze, and the patina-value referral default

competency_questions.question: What must be disclosed to and signed by the customer before irreversible work on their piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPECTATION_DISCLOSURE covers plated-never-solid honesty, wear-life-as-mechanism talk, and unachievable outcomes said early; IRREVERSIBILITY_SIGNOFF requires specific written consent per irreversible step and re-consent on scope change

competency_questions.question: What exactly does the prep line receive from triage, and how does a misidentification show up downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBSTRATE_ROUTE_CARD defines the facts-and-flags handoff artifact and the incomplete-card hard stop; MISID_FAILURE_MAP maps each triage miss to its downstream failure signature and back

competency_questions.question: What safety obligations govern the assessment bench and its test chemicals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSESSMENT_BENCH_SAFETY states the commercial-product-per-instructions rule, labeled segregated storage, the absolute cyanide-acid separation line, regulated disposal, and the formal-training and jurisdiction-check obligations

competency_questions.question: What is nickel's significance at triage for skin-contact jewelry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICKEL_CONTACT_FLAG identifies likely nickel in arriving pieces, records skin-contact status against the nickel-release regulation class with a verify-jurisdiction pointer, and routes allergy questions to professional care

glossary.definition: Cheap zinc-alloy castings common in costume jewelry, trophies, and buckles; light for their bulk, porous, attacked by aggressive cleaners and acids, and prone to internal corrosion with age - the highest-risk substrate family a plating bench receives.

A struck mark asserting fineness, maker, origin, or construction class; at triage it is a documented claim that steers testing and creates a preservation obligation, never by itself proof of identity.

Minimally destructive identification using a commercial jeweler's test-kit reagent on a hidden point per the product's instructions; it reads the surface it touches, so on plated goods it reports the coating unless the core is deliberately exposed with documented consent.

Mechanically clad constructions whose skin is genuine wrought karat alloy bonded at the mill, marked by weight-fraction conventions such as 1/20 14K GF; the skin is finite, buffing through it is unrepairable, and no electroplate restores the construction.

Historical mercury-amalgam gilding; antique fire-gilt bronze can retain residual mercury, so it is never torched, stripped, or ultrasonically cleaned at an ordinary shop - conservation referral is the only correct route.

The self-healing chromium-oxide skin on stainless steel that reforms within seconds in air; its presence is why a stainless identification forks the piece toward the chemical line's dedicated activation-and-strike class instead of the mild-steel path.

A stone whose brilliance depends on a reflective foil behind it; any liquid reaching the foil ruins it permanently, so foil-backs never enter wet processes and usually force removal, a selective-process flag, or refusal.

The document that accompanies a piece through the shop carrying its verified identity, coating map, risk flags, verdict, conditions, and sign-offs - the intake bench's product and the only interface downstream benches consume.
The verdict class for pieces that may proceed only under named, documented, customer-acknowledged risk conditions, each tied to a specific flag on the route card.

A family of identification methods - magnet, weight and feel, hallmark reading, spot test, surface-instrument reads - used as corroborating evidence classes under the two-agreeing-methods rule rather than as single-method verdicts.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for gold_plating_substrate_triage work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix the operating rule of the intake bench: no piece touches a wheel, an ultrasonic, or any tank until it has been identified, risk-surveyed, and given an explicit accept, accept-with-conditions, refuse, or refer verdict. The mandate exists because most plating failures are prep failures, and almost every catastrophic loss on customer goods - a dissolved pot-metal casting, a ruined pearl, a stripped antique patina - happens when chemistry or the wheel starts before assessment finishes; the triage bench is the one point in the shop where an irreversible mistake can still be declined. The mandate also assigns authority: the assessor may refuse work regardless of commercial pressure, and nobody downstream may override a refusal by simply starting the job.

included: the four verdict classes as the bench's vocabulary
refusal authority and its protection from sales pressure
excluded: the verdict criteria themselves (the integration node)
commercial handling of a refusal (business specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a bypass incident or a shop-loss postmortem shows the gate is porous or wrongly placed

pros.claim: A hard no-work-before-verdict rule converts unknown-substrate disasters into declined jobs
pros.example: a die-cast trophy figure that would have foamed apart in the soak cleaner is refused at the bench instead of dissolving in the tank

cons.claim: An absolute gate adds queue time to trivially safe work
cons.example: a plain new brass cuff from a known trade account still waits for a recorded verdict before the line may take it

failure_modes: rush jobs routed straight to the polishing wheel with triage backfilled later
verdict authority quietly eroded because a refusal was overridden once and it became precedent
the mandate treated as paperwork rather than the point where losses are actually prevented
acceptance_tests: the posted shop rule names all four verdict classes, states that no chemistry or wheel work precedes a recorded verdict, and assigns refusal authority to the assessor in writing
revisit_triggers: a loss event reaches a tank or wheel that the mandate should have intercepted
queue records show pieces entering the line without a verdict entry

nodes.definition: Ask before testing: where the piece came from, what the customer believes it is, prior repairs or replating, whether it is worn against skin daily, what outcome they want (color, coverage, make-it-like-new), and whether it carries sentimental or heirloom weight. Everything the customer says is captured as a claim to verify, never as a fact - 'solid gold', 'it just needs a dip', and 'there are no repairs' are the three statements most often falsified at the bench. The interview also surfaces constraints no test can see, such as a pearl restrung by a relative or a nickel sensitivity in the household, and it fixes the service goal the eventual verdict must be measured against.

excluded: pricing and quoting (business specialist)
verifying the claims (the test ladder does that)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurring bench surprises of a kind an added interview question would have surfaced

pros.claim: A good interview steers testing toward the piece's actual weak points
pros.example: a customer mentioning a ring was resized cheaply once sends the assessor straight to the shank joint hunting for soft solder

cons.claim: Customer accounts anchor the assessor and bias ambiguous readings
cons.example: hearing that grandfather bought it as 14 karat makes a faint worn stamp read as a fineness mark when it is actually a plated-goods mark

failure_modes: customer statements recorded as facts instead of claims
the heirloom question skipped, leaving sentimental catastrophe exposure undiscovered until after damage
the service goal never pinned down, so the verdict cannot say whether the requested job is even the right service
acceptance_tests: the interview record separates claims from observations and contains provenance, prior work, skin-contact use, service goal, and heirloom weight for every customer piece
revisit_triggers: a mid-job surprise traces to a question the interview script never asks

nodes.definition: Examine the piece under a loupe and strong light before any reagent or tool touches it, and photograph it first: overall construction (cast, stamped, assembled, hollow or solid), every joint and finding, the existing finish and its wear pattern, damage, prior-repair evidence such as color mismatch at joints or newer-looking solder, suspicious seams or plugs, and where the marks sit. The examination produces the baseline condition record - dated photographs plus a written condition note - that all later sign-offs, disputes, and before-and-after comparisons hang from, and it builds the physical map (joints here, stones there, hollow sections there) that every subsequent risk-zone survey works through.

included: the written baseline record and physical map
excluded: identification tests (the ladder)
any cleaning to see better - the piece is examined as received

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dispute outcomes or missed-feature incidents implicating the examination checklist or its lighting and loupe discipline

pros.claim: Photographing before first touch makes later disputes decidable on evidence
pros.example: a customer certain the shop dented a locket is answered by the intake photograph showing the dent on arrival

cons.claim: Examination quality rides on the assessor's eye and light, and it spends bench minutes on every piece
cons.example: a hairline crack in a hollow bangle missed under poor light lets the piece flood with solution later

failure_modes: handling or wiping the piece before the photographs exist
condition notes so generic they prove nothing in a dispute
construction read wrong - hollow taken for solid - so every later survey starts from a false map
acceptance_tests: every customer piece has dated arrival photographs and a condition note that names construction, joints, finish state, damage, and mark locations before any test result appears in the file
revisit_triggers: a dispute or mid-job discovery exposes a class of feature the examination checklist does not cover

nodes.definition: Order identification methods as an escalation ladder and never assume identity from appearance: first the free non-contact reads (color, wear pattern, construction logic, marks), then the non-destructive physical screens (magnet classes, weight-for-bulk feel), then instrument reads where available (an XRF-class surface-alloy reading, with its known blindness to construction), and only then minimally destructive chemistry - a spot test on a hidden point - or a consented sacrificial cut. Two independent method classes must agree before a substrate family is assigned; a single-method identification is recorded as provisional. The ladder exists because every downstream chain forks on identity, and because the cheap early rungs falsify most wrong guesses before anything irreversible happens.

included: the escalation order and its rationale
when destructive rungs are justified and consented
excluded: execution detail of each screen (their own nodes)
line-side cleanliness tests such as the water-break gate (chemical-prep KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: misidentification postmortems or a change in available method classes that reorders the ladder's cost-certainty tradeoff

pros.claim: The two-agreeing-methods rule catches the misreads any single screen lets through
pros.example: a white-metal pendant a magnet suggests is stainless is caught by heft plus a spot test as nickel-plated brass before the line treats it as passive steel

cons.claim: The full ladder is disproportionate for routine trade lots and slows the bench
cons.example: fifty identical new castings from a regular manufacturer need lot-level verification, not fifty ladders

failure_modes: appearance-only identification under queue pressure
jumping to the destructive rung because it is decisive, skipping cheaper screens that would have sufficed
ladder results unrecorded so the family assignment cannot be audited later
acceptance_tests: every family assignment in the file cites at least two agreeing method classes or is explicitly marked provisional
no destructive test appears in a file without the exhausted-ladder note and, where visible or core-exposing, documented consent
revisit_triggers: a downstream failure traces to an identification the ladder passed
a new instrument or test kit class becomes available to the bench

nodes.definition: Run the zero-cost physical screens and read them as classes, never as verdicts: a strong magnet pull says iron-steel family; no pull rules steel out but rules nothing in; a faint pull warns of a nickel layer or a work-hardened stainless without proving either; weight-for-bulk sorts the light zinc die-cast feel from the dense brass and silver feel and flags anomalously heavy filled or weighted pieces; temperature-on-lip and ring-tone are supporting cues only. The screen's whole value is speed at the top of the ladder: in seconds it forks the piece toward the right confirmation tests and flags the contradictions - a magnetic 'silver' figurine, a featherweight 'bronze' - that demand escalation instead of a shrug.

included: magnet response classes and their honest ambiguity
excluded: chemical and instrument identification (their own nodes)
any conclusion drawn from a single cue

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a screen-attributed misread cluster or a new quick screen worth adding to the top rungs

pros.claim: Seconds of screening catch category errors before any chemistry is considered
pros.example: a silver-look figurine that snaps to the magnet is diverted to steel-family confirmation instead of a misleading silver spot test

cons.claim: Single-cue readings mislead exactly where plated goods are common
cons.example: heavy nickel plate over brass gives a faint magnetic pull that a hurried assessor books as stainless

failure_modes: a magnet result treated as an identity verdict
the heft comparison skipped on castings, missing the die-cast lightness cue
a contradictory screen left unrecorded, so the ambiguity never forces escalation
acceptance_tests: screen entries record the cue, the reading, and the class interpretation, and contradictory screens carry an explicit escalation note
revisit_triggers: a misread traced to a screen cue whose class interpretation needs sharpening

nodes.definition: Find, transcribe, and interpret every mark before deciding anything: fineness numbers and karat marks, silver standard marks, plated-goods marks of the electroplate classes, gold-filled and rolled-gold fraction marks of the 1/20 14K GF convention, maker and assay-office marks, and origin cues that date and place the piece. A mark is a claim struck by someone else, not a test result: marks guide which tests to run and raise the stakes of the verdict - an assay-marked antique or a fraction-marked clad piece must not be treated as generic plate - but counterfeit and misapplied marks exist, so no mark stands against a contradicting physical test. Reading also creates an obligation: a transcribed mark is now a documented feature that later mechanical work must not soften or remove without sign-off.

included: the preservation obligation a read mark creates
excluded: legal marking compliance for outgoing goods (compliance specialist)
the physical tests that confirm or refute a mark

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an encountered mark class the reading guide does not cover, or a counterfeit pattern circulating in the trade

pros.claim: Fraction and plated-goods marks reroute the whole job when read early
pros.example: spotting 1/20 12K GF on a bracelet clasp cancels a planned cut-down buff that would have broken through the rolled-gold skin

cons.claim: Worn, tiny, or transplanted marks are easy to misread, and marks migrate between assembled parts
cons.example: a marked 925 clasp soldered onto a plated chain makes the whole chain read sterling if the assessor stops at the first mark found

failure_modes: a mark quoted to the customer as proof of identity
marks hidden under findings or inside bands never found
polishing plans made before the marks are transcribed, so nobody prices the preservation constraint
acceptance_tests: the mark transcript lists every found mark with location and a class interpretation, each tagged verify-pending until a physical test agrees
revisit_triggers: a counterfeit or transplanted mark reaches the verdict stage before being caught

nodes.definition: When the non-destructive rungs leave identity ambiguous, apply a commercial jeweler's test kit exactly per its instructions on the least visible point of the piece - inside a shank, under a clasp, on the back of a finding - and only after the organics survey has cleared the area of anything a drop could wick into. Spot testing is mildly destructive by nature: it can leave a mark, and on plated goods it reads the coating unless a consented notch or file point exposes the core, so visible-location testing and any core-exposing step require the customer's documented consent first. Results are recorded with location, product used, and reading, and are interpreted as class evidence feeding the family assignment, never as a standalone verdict.

included: hidden-point selection after the organics check
consent rules for visible or core-exposing tests
excluded: reagent formulation of any kind
prep-line chemistry (chemical-prep KB)
assay-grade fineness determination (referred out)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: kit instruction revisions, a consent dispute, or a wrong-reading incident tied to reagent condition

pros.claim: A spot test settles what magnet and heft cannot
pros.example: distinguishing silver-plated copper from solid silver on an unmarked candlestick base

cons.claim: On plated or clad goods the surface answer is systematically wrong about the core
cons.example: a drop on gold-filled stock reads karat gold and says nothing about the brass beneath it

failure_modes: testing on a visible face without consent
testing over or near a glued stone, pearl, or foil-back the drop can reach
reagent used past its service life or off-instructions, giving a confident wrong answer
a result recorded without its location, so a later dispute about the mark cannot be answered
acceptance_tests: every spot-test entry records product, location, reading, and the organics-cleared note; visible-location and core-exposing tests carry documented consent
revisit_triggers: a kit product change or a reading pattern suggesting degraded reagents

nodes.definition: Bind the assessment bench to the same obligation classes as the rest of the shop even though its chemistry is drop-scale: test reagents are commercial products stored, labeled, and used per their instructions and safety data sheets; acids at the bench live in their own labeled, contained storage, absolutely segregated from any cyanide-bearing process anywhere on the premises - cyanide solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together, and never share a drain; eye protection and gloves are worn for reagent work; spent test materials go to the shop's regulated waste stream, never the sink; and the assessor's competence rests on formal training, with the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules verified rather than assumed. The bench holds no self-mixed chemistry of any kind.

included: reagent storage, labeling, PPE, and disposal obligation classes
the absolute cyanide-acid segregation line as it touches the bench
excluded: shop-wide safety program and waste manifesting (safety specialist)
process-tank safety (line KBs)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an audit finding, incident, or rule change in the jurisdiction's workplace or hazmat requirements

pros.claim: Treating the small test bottles with full discipline removes the shop's easiest route to a segregation breach
pros.example: a test-acid bottle can never be dropped near a cyanide-line drain if segregated bench placement makes it impossible for one to be there

cons.claim: Full segregation and logging feels disproportionate at drop scale and invites quiet shortcuts
cons.example: an assessor keeping an unlabeled decanted dropper in a drawer because the proper cabinet is across the room

failure_modes: unlabeled decanted reagents accumulating at the bench
test acids stored with or routed past cyanide-bearing areas
spent swabs and neutralized drops flushed to a drain
reagent work by staff without the formal training the products assume
acceptance_tests: a bench audit finds every reagent commercial, labeled, and in segregated contained storage away from any cyanide-bearing area, a documented disposal route, current training records, and a dated jurisdiction rule check
revisit_triggers: a near-miss, a reagent product change, or a jurisdiction rule update touching the bench

nodes.definition: Assign every accepted piece to a base-metal family - brass/bronze/copper, silver, zinc die-cast/pot metal, mild or carbon steel, stainless steel, or an unknown white metal held for further work - because the family, not the piece's look, decides everything downstream: which activation class the chemical line keys on, whether a passive film must be defeated (stainless repassivates within seconds, the corpus-grounded fact the line's strike class exists for), whether acid exposure is survivable at all (pot metal often cannot survive it), whether diffusion threatens thin gold without a barrier (the silver and brass classes), and whether hydrogen-embrittlement caution applies (the spring-steel class). The assignment is made only on two agreeing method classes, recorded with its evidence, and an honest 'unknown, held' always beats a plausible guess.

included: the family taxonomy and each family's triage consequence
excluded: executing the downstream activation or strike (chemical-prep KB)
alloy-grade metallurgy beyond what triage needs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: line feedback showing a family's stated consequence was wrong or incomplete for pieces actually received

pros.claim: The family assignment is the single highest-leverage fact on the route card
pros.example: writing stainless instead of mild steel on the card is the difference between a bonded deposit and whole-stack peeling at the line

cons.claim: Family classes blur at the edges where alloys and platings overlap
cons.example: nickel silver contains no silver and behaves as its own problem, and a leaded brass casting pits unlike wrought brass

failure_modes: assignment from color alone
unknowns silently defaulted to brass because brass is the common case
a family recorded without its evidence pair, so the call can never be audited
acceptance_tests: every family entry names its two agreeing method classes or carries the unknown-held flag
each family entry lists the downstream fork it triggers so the route card can carry the flag
revisit_triggers: a downstream adhesion or dissolution failure implicating a family call
a new substrate class starts arriving that the taxonomy does not cover

nodes.definition: Treat zinc die-cast/pot metal as the highest-risk family at the bench and triage it explicitly: recognize it by the cast-seam look, soft tool-bright scratches, light heft for its bulk, and its typical product classes (costume jewelry, trophies, belt buckles, cheap findings), then decide whether the individual piece can survive any wet route at all. Pot metal reacts with aggressive cleaners and acids, gasses through its porosity, and old castings can be corroded internally to the point of crumbling under modest handling; previous plate can hide all of this. The outcome is one of three: accept with a documented fragile-substrate condition and a pot-metal routing flag, refuse because the casting is already deteriorating, or refer where the piece's value justifies a specialist restorer instead of a plating line.

included: the survival decision and its three outcomes
excluded: the special prep chemistry a surviving piece gets (chemical-prep KB per its TDS discipline)
restoration technique (referred out)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a survival misjudgment in either direction - a refused piece proven sound elsewhere, or an accepted casting lost

pros.claim: Naming pot metal at intake converts the classic dissolved-in-the-cleaner disaster into a managed decision
pros.example: a 1930s die-cast car mascot with bubbling old plate is refused with photographs instead of coming out of the soak tank as gray sponge

cons.claim: The recognition cues are probabilistic and previous plate masks them
cons.example: a chrome-look plate over die-cast passes color and scratch checks until a hidden-spot notch shows gray crystalline metal

failure_modes: pot metal assumed to be brass because it was plated yellow
an accepted fragile casting entering the line without its routing flag
an aged casting handled firmly during examination and cracking at the bench itself
acceptance_tests: every die-cast identification includes a survival judgment with named evidence and one of the three outcomes; accepted pieces carry the fragile-substrate condition and routing flag
revisit_triggers: a pot-metal piece degrading at the line despite an accept verdict

nodes.definition: Establish what already covers the piece, because the coating is what every surface test touches first and what the job must either build on or remove: previous gold plate and its wear-through pattern, nickel or silver layers showing as color steps at high-wear points, chrome-look finishes, lacquers and anti-tarnish organic coatings that shrug off polish and block deposition, painted or filled recesses, and hard vacuum-coating classes that no bench chemistry touches. The identification is evidential - wear windows where the layer stack shows in section, color transitions, how a hidden-spot solvent swab or scratch behaves - and its output is a coating map: what is on the piece, where it is worn through, and what that implies for tests (surface reads are the coating, not the core) and for the strip-or-overplate decision that belongs to the line and finishing benches.

included: the surface-read caveat it imposes on all tests
excluded: performing any strip (line territory, with its own approvals)
choosing the new stack (process specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: coating-attributed line surprises or a shift in the coating classes arriving with customer goods

pros.claim: Reading wear-through windows turns a worn piece into a free cross-section
pros.example: a ring's high spot showing white metal under yellow reveals a nickel layer beneath plate before any instrument is used

cons.claim: Coatings frustrate identification precisely because they cover everything the tests want to reach
cons.example: an even lacquer coat defeats both spot test and surface instrument until a hidden-point swab finds it

failure_modes: surface readings recorded as core identity
lacquer discovered only when nothing responds at the line
a hard vacuum-coating finish mistaken for plate and promised strippable
acceptance_tests: the coating map names each detected layer with its evidence, marks wear-through locations, and states what the map forbids the tests to conclude about the core
revisit_triggers: a line report of unexpected behavior under the first tank implicating an unmapped coating
a new coating class starts appearing on incoming goods

nodes.definition: Decide, with stated confidence, whether the piece is solid precious alloy through its section, mechanically clad (the gold-filled and rolled-gold classes, whose skin is genuine wrought karat alloy in the microns-to-tens-of-microns class), or electroplated (thin coating classes over base metal), because the three constructions have opposite triage consequences: solid tolerates rework, clad has a finite skin that buffing breaks through and no replate truly restores, and plated goods are the shop's normal work. Surface instruments cannot make this call alone - an XRF-class reading reports the skin's alloy and is blind to what lies beneath, a corpus-grounded limit - so the verdict is assembled from marks and their fraction conventions, edge and wear evidence, density feel, and where justified a consented sacrificial cut; where evidence stays thin the class is recorded as undetermined and the piece is handled to the most protective assumption.

included: the solid / clad / plated taxonomy and consequences
evidence assembly and the undetermined class
excluded: destructive assay technique (referred to assay-class services)
marking-law thresholds for outgoing claims (compliance specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a construction misclass reaching the wheel or the customer, or new instrument access changing what is decidable non-destructively

pros.claim: The construction verdict prevents two symmetric disasters: buffing through clad skin and replating a solid heirloom nobody needed to plate
pros.example: wear-through showing brass at a bracelet clasp edge proves not-solid and stops a just-polish-it-deeper plan

cons.claim: Without destructive evidence the call is sometimes genuinely unavailable
cons.example: heavy vintage plate and worn gold-filled stock can present identically at the surface; only a consented cut or a declared undetermined class is honest

failure_modes: a surface karat reading reported to the customer as proof of solid gold
undetermined pieces silently worked as plated because that is the default job
fraction marks ignored because the skin tested as karat alloy
acceptance_tests: every construction verdict lists its evidence, states its confidence, and undetermined pieces carry the most-protective-assumption handling note
revisit_triggers: a construction call reversed by later evidence mid-job

nodes.definition: Walk every joint on the piece and classify it, because joints are where heat, chemistry, and mechanical work concentrate their damage: original high-temperature gold or silver brazed joints are generally robust, while low-temperature lead-tin soft solder - the signature of cheap repairs - shows as a gray, soft, low-luster seam that darkens in chemistry, plates over poorly, and melts far below any brazing temperature; unknown repair joints inherit the worst assumption. The survey also notes structural role: a joint holding a bail or a hinge is a failure that loses the piece, not a blemish. Output is a joint map with a vulnerability class per joint, feeding the verdict (soft-soldered pieces are accept-with-conditions at best), the route card's caution flags, and the line's awareness that lead-bearing solder is a bath-contamination concern as a class.

included: structural-role flagging and the joint map
excluded: re-soldering or joint repair (referred to a jeweler)
how the line manages contamination (its own KBs)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missed-joint incident or a repair style trend (new adhesive or solder classes) in incoming goods

pros.claim: Finding the soft-solder repair at intake reprices the risk before the shop owns it
pros.example: a gray seam at a chain's clasp ring downgrades the job to accept-with-conditions with the joint photographed and disclaimed

cons.claim: Good repairs are nearly invisible and plate hides seams
cons.example: a soft-soldered bail under old gold plate shows only as a faint color step a loupe can miss

failure_modes: joints inventoried on the display side only
soft solder discovered by the line when it darkens in the first tank
structural joints not distinguished from decorative ones, so a bail failure surprises everyone
acceptance_tests: the joint map covers every joint on the piece with a class and structural-role note, and any unknown repair joint carries the worst-assumption flag
revisit_triggers: a joint failure or joint discoloration downstream that the survey did not flag

nodes.definition: Inventory everything on the piece that is not metal and give each item a disposition before any route is discussed, under the default rule that stones, pearls, and organics do not enter tanks: identify the settings (prong and bezel work may allow professional removal; glue-set and foil-backed stones are destroyed by heat, solvents, ultrasonic agitation, or any liquid reaching the foil) and the materials by vulnerability class - pearls, coral, shell, amber, jet, ivory-class materials, turquoise, opal, and enamel are attacked or crazed by acids, heat, and ultrasonic energy, and oiled emerald-class stones lose their treatment in solvents. Dispositions are: remove professionally and reset after plating, mask only where a competent assessor judges genuine isolation achievable, flag for a selective or brush-class process decided downstream, or refuse and refer; sentimental value weights every call toward the conservative end.

included: the four dispositions and the conservative default
excluded: unsetting and resetting handwork (referred to a setter)
executing selective or brush plating (process specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an organics loss or near-miss, or a new stone-treatment class arriving that changes a vulnerability rating

pros.claim: The organics-first rule prevents the least reversible category of loss at the bench
pros.example: an heirloom pearl ring goes for professional stone removal and reset instead of gambling the pearl on masking tape

cons.claim: Removal and reset add cost and their own handling risk, which tempts everyone toward masking
cons.example: a tight pave field quoted for full unset-and-reset makes the customer balk at the price of doing it right

failure_modes: closed-back settings never opened for inspection, so a foil or glue surprise emerges mid-job
masking treated as the default rather than the exception
enamel not recognized as carrying organic-class vulnerability
acceptance_tests: every non-metal element appears in the inventory with a material class, a setting class, and one recorded disposition before any verdict is issued
revisit_triggers: any stone, pearl, or organic damaged in-shop, however minor

nodes.definition: Find the zones that will trap, hide, or leak before anyone imagines the piece in a tank: casting porosity that outgasses and later weeps solution as stain and corrosion; hollow construction - beads, bangles, spouts, handles, lockets - whose vents and pinholes flood and cannot be verifiably emptied; crimped and folded seams that wick; and filled construction - pitch- or cement-loaded hollowware, weighted bases, filled knife handles - where heat or immersion breaches the fill or the fill contaminates whatever it touches. Findings feed the verdict directly: some traps only demand routing and drying flags, but an unverifiable internal void or a filled body is routinely a refusal or a referral, because trapped chemistry keeps working on the piece for weeks after it goes home.

included: the weep and fill-breach mechanisms as triage facts
excluded: rinse and drying procedure at the line (chemical-prep KB)
repairing or venting hollow work (referred out)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-handover weep incidents or a construction class (new hollow goods trend) the survey underestimates

pros.claim: Trap-hunting at intake prevents the delayed failure the customer discovers on a shelf weeks later
pros.example: a hollow bead necklace with pinholes is refused for immersion routes, so the weep-stain three weeks later never happens

cons.claim: Internal voids are only partially observable from outside
cons.example: a soldered-shut hollow bangle gives no external sign whether it is dry, internally cracked, or already holding another shop's old pickle

failure_modes: a weight anomaly never checked against construction, reading a filled base as thick casting
vents assumed to drain because they flooded
porosity noted but no routing or drying flag issued, so the note changes nothing
acceptance_tests: every hollow, porous, seamed, or filled zone is mapped with its trap mechanism and either a flag or a refusal-referral ground attached
revisit_triggers: a weep, stain, or fill-breach report after handover

nodes.definition: Screen every old piece for the two properties that take it off the bench entirely: mercury fire gilding and conservation value. Ormolu and other fire-gilt work - typical of pre-industrial and nineteenth-century gilt bronze - can retain residual mercury in its gilding, so torching, stripping, or ultrasonic work on antique gilt bronze is prohibited in an ordinary shop as a corpus-grounded hazard class; the recognition cues (age, object class, the soft matte-and-burnished gilt look) justify referral, and no bench test should try to prove mercury's presence. Independently, patina, original surface, and maker evidence carry collector value that any replate destroys, so an antique's default verdict is refer - to a conservator for gilt bronze, to a specialist restorer where value is plausible - with the reasoning documented; replating an antique happens only after the owner has been told in writing what it erases.

included: fire-gilt recognition cues and the hazard-class prohibition
the default-refer rule and its documentation
excluded: conservation treatment itself (conservator territory)
valuation and appraisal (referred to the trade)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: conservation guidance updates or a screen miss on a genuine fire-gilt or high-value antique

pros.claim: The default-refer rule removes a health hazard and a value-destruction liability in one screen
pros.example: a gilt bronze clock case brought in for brightening goes to a conservator with a written note instead of into the ultrasonic

cons.claim: Over-triggering the screen sends ordinary old-but-worthless plate away needlessly
cons.example: a mass-produced 1960s gilt casting is not ormolu, and referring it wastes the customer's time and the shop's job

failure_modes: age cues ignored because the customer only asked for a polish
mercury risk investigated by bench experiment instead of referral
patina stripped on a verbal okay nobody wrote down
acceptance_tests: every piece with age cues has a screen entry; suspected fire-gilt items show a documented referral and never an in-shop torch, strip, or ultrasonic step
revisit_triggers: a conservator's report contradicting the screen's call in either direction

nodes.definition: Flag at triage every piece where nickel is present or would foreseeably be added, because skin-contact jewelry faces nickel-release limits as a regulation class (EN 1811-class testing under EU REACH-class rules is the corpus-grounded example; the selling jurisdiction's current rules must be verified): identify likely nickel in what arrives - nickel-silver base metal, bright white underlayers showing at wear-through, unknown white metals - and record whether the piece is worn against skin (earring posts and backs, rings, bracelets) so the downstream stack choice can respect the compliance class or the customer can be pointed to nickel-free options. Customer mentions of metal allergy are routed to the regulation class and to professional medical care, never answered as medical advice; the flag is a compliance and routing fact, not a diagnosis.

included: the verify-jurisdiction compliance flag and the medical-care routing rule
excluded: stack design and nickel-free alternatives selection (process specialist)
release testing itself (send-out class)
any medical judgment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulation-class change in any selling jurisdiction the shop serves, or a reaction complaint tied to shop output

pros.claim: Catching the nickel question at intake keeps compliance a design input instead of a handover surprise
pros.example: an earring replate order flagged skin-contact lets the line start its stack decision from the nickel-release class rather than discovering it at pickup

cons.claim: Nickel presence in an arriving piece is often unprovable at the bench
cons.example: a white underlayer at a wear window may be nickel or a white-bronze class, and the flag can only record the uncertainty

failure_modes: skin-contact status never asked at intake
an allergy question answered as medical advice instead of routed to care
the flag recorded in the file but never carried onto the route card
acceptance_tests: every skin-contact piece shows a nickel note (present, suspected, unknown) and the flag appears on the route card with its verify-jurisdiction pointer
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction rule change on nickel release or a customer reaction report

nodes.definition: Maintain the explicit map from triage misses to the downstream failures they cause, because the map is both the assessor's motivation and the shop's diagnostic dictionary: stainless read as mild steel produces whole-stack peeling because the passive film was never defeated; pot metal read as brass produces foaming, pitting, or a dissolved piece in cleaners and acids; a missed lacquer produces a piece nothing deposits on; missed soft solder produces a joint that darkens or melts; a missed foil-back or glued stone produces a destroyed stone; and bare steel misrouted toward acid-class baths produces the classic zero-adhesion immersion deposit the strike class exists to prevent. When the quality bench traces a failure to one of these signatures, the map points back to the specific triage step that missed, closing the loop that keeps the ladder honest.

included: briefing new assessors from the map
excluded: full defect diagnosis across chemistry and process causes (quality specialist)
fixing the failures (line and finishing benches)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unmapped failure signature appearing at the quality bench or a mapped signature proving to have a different dominant cause

pros.claim: The map turns downstream defects into targeted triage fixes instead of general blame
pros.example: a peeling batch traced to one magnetic-screen shortcut tightens that screen for white metals shop-wide

cons.claim: The map covers known signatures only and can misattribute novel failures
cons.example: a peel caused by a line-side rinse lapse gets pinned on identification if the map is treated as the only suspect list

failure_modes: failures logged without a triage-cause hypothesis
the map never briefed to new assessors, so each one relearns it by loss
the same miss recurring because the loop back to the ladder stayed informal
acceptance_tests: each catalog entry pairs a triage miss with its downstream signature and the ladder step that owns it
revisit_triggers: a downstream failure with no matching signature in the map
quality-bench feedback reclassifying a mapped signature's usual cause

nodes.definition: Integrate everything the assessment produced - the family assignment with its evidence pair, coating map, construction class, joint map, organics dispositions, trap findings, and antique screen - into one of four verdicts with named grounds: accept (identity verified, construction sound, no vulnerable element unresolved), accept-with-conditions (specific documented risks the customer has acknowledged, each tied to a condition on the route card), refuse (the piece cannot survive the service, or the shop cannot bound the risk honestly), or refer (conservator, stone setter for removal and reset, assay-class verification, or a better-equipped shop). The verdict cites its grounds so it can be audited and defended; refusal is a complete and honorable outcome delivered with the reason and alternatives, and no commercial pressure converts a refuse into an accept - a lost job costs a fee, a lost heirloom costs the shop's name.

included: the integration of all survey outputs
the four verdict classes with named grounds
refusal and referral delivery with documentation
excluded: commercial consequences of the verdict (business specialist)
the surveys themselves (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verdict-outcome mismatches in either direction accumulating in the shop log

pros.claim: Named-grounds verdicts make the bench auditable and the refusals defensible
pros.example: a refusal citing crumbling die-cast with photographs survives the angry-customer conversation; a bare no would not

cons.claim: Conservative verdicts carry a real cost in refused revenue and referred customers
cons.example: a run of cautious refer verdicts on merely-old costume pieces sends paying work to a competitor

failure_modes: verdicts issued before the risk surveys finish
accept-with-conditions used as a pressure valve with conditions nobody reads
refusal grounds left unrecorded, inviting the dispute they should have closed
acceptance_tests: every verdict entry cites the family evidence, the relevant survey outputs, and its named grounds; every condition on an accept-with-conditions maps to a route-card flag
revisit_triggers: an accepted piece failing for a cause a survey had flagged
refusal-rate drift suggesting the criteria have gone too loose or too tight

nodes.definition: Before any step that cannot be undone on a customer piece, obtain specific, written, informed consent: polishing through existing plate to reach the metal beneath, work that will soften detail or shallow engraving, any risk to a transcribed hallmark, stone removal, core-exposing test cuts, and stripping of existing finishes. The sign-off names the exact step, the reason, the realistic risk - including the possibility that what lies underneath is not what anyone hopes - and what cannot be restored afterward; a signature gathered by accurate description is protection, one gathered by minimizing is liability. Verbal agreement, however enthusiastic, authorizes nothing irreversible; the signed record joins the route card, and any scope change mid-job returns the piece to this gate before the added work proceeds.

included: specific written consent content and timing
excluded: performing the irreversible work (finishing bench, per its own limits)
liability and contract terms (business specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute outcome or jurisdictional consumer-rule change touching consent documentation

pros.claim: Specific consent converts the worst conversations from accusations into confirmations
pros.example: when buffed-through plate reveals gray pot metal, the signed note predicting exactly that possibility ends the dispute before it starts

cons.claim: Consent friction is real and reads as bureaucracy to a trusting customer
cons.example: a trade jeweler impatient at signing per-step authorizations for a routine strip-and-replate lot

failure_modes: blanket authorizations covering unnamed steps
sign-off text minimizing the risk to close the sale
scope creep mid-job proceeding on the original signature
acceptance_tests: every irreversible step in a job file maps to a signed authorization naming that step, its risk, and what cannot be restored; scope changes show a fresh signature
revisit_triggers: a consent dispute or a mid-job stop caused by missing authorization

nodes.definition: Before acceptance is final, tell the customer what the service actually delivers and record that it was told: plated is a coating and is never represented as solid gold; wear life is a function of thickness class, use, and skin chemistry, discussed as ranges and mechanisms rather than promised in years; replating restores color and coverage but does not restore lost detail, does not erase deep scratches (that is metal removal, with its own sign-off), and does not turn a worn gold-filled skin back into gold-filled; and some wanted outcomes - an antique's original fire-gilt glow, factory-identical color on an unknown vintage stack - may be honestly unachievable and are said so at the bench, not at handover. The disclosure record protects both sides and is the ethical floor of the trade: no piece is represented as something it is not.

included: unachievable-outcome candor and the disclosure record
excluded: price and warranty terms (business specialist)
marking-law claim wording on outgoing goods (compliance specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: handover-dispute patterns or trade-rule changes about representations of plated goods

pros.claim: Expectation honesty at intake is cheaper than disappointment at handover
pros.example: a customer told a thin flash refresh is cosmetic and will wear at pressure points either upgrades informed or accepts the limits informed

cons.claim: Honest disclosure loses some jobs a softer pitch would have kept
cons.example: a customer promised miracles by a competitor takes the piece there after hearing what replating cannot do

failure_modes: wear life promised in confident years
solid-gold language from the customer left standing uncorrected
disclosure delivered verbally and never recorded
acceptance_tests: every accepted job shows a disclosure record covering coating-not-solid status, wear expectation as a mechanism, and any unachievable requested outcome named before acceptance
revisit_triggers: a handover dispute rooted in an expectation the record never addressed

nodes.definition: Compile the triage outcome into the route card - the traveler that physically accompanies the piece and is the only interface the finishing bench and chemical line consume: verified substrate family with its evidence pair, coating map and construction class, joint map with vulnerability flags, organics dispositions, trap and drying flags, the pot-metal and passive-substrate routing flags the line keys its activation and strike classes on, the nickel and skin-contact compliance flag, the verdict with its conditions, and the sign-offs attached. The card states facts and flags, never process parameters - which compounds, chemistries, and setpoints to use belongs to the finishing and line KBs and their TDS discipline - and an incomplete card is a hard stop: the line may refuse any piece whose card does not answer its forks, and a card reading 'unknown, held' is a legitimate card while a guessed entry is not.

included: the card's required fields and flag set
the incomplete-card hard stop and the line's right of refusal
excluded: process parameters, compound choices, and chemistry (sibling KBs per their TDS discipline)
job pricing fields (business specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream benches requesting fields or flags the card does not carry, or ignoring fields it does

pros.claim: A complete card makes every downstream fork a lookup instead of a re-investigation
pros.example: the line reads the stainless flag and keys its passive-substrate class without re-deriving the metallurgy at the tank

cons.claim: Cards ossify errors with authority - a wrong card is worse than no card
cons.example: a guessed brass entry sails through the line's checks precisely because the card is trusted

failure_modes: cards issued with empty fields to keep the queue moving
flags living in the assessor's head instead of on the card
the card separated from the piece mid-shop
acceptance_tests: no piece leaves triage without a card carrying family plus evidence, coating and construction entries, all risk flags, the verdict with conditions, and attached sign-offs; unknowns are written as unknown-held, never guessed
revisit_triggers: a line-side rejection or query showing the card's field set does not answer a downstream fork
sibling-KB changes that add a fork the card must feed

edges.why_related: the examination exists because the mandate forbids any work before assessment
interview claims tell the examiner where to look first (repairs, restrung pearls, resized shanks)
the ladder escalates from the examination's map; testing an unexamined piece risks the very features triage protects
the physical screens are the ladder's cheap top rungs, run in the order the ladder fixes
mark reading is the ladder's free non-contact rung and steers which later rungs are worth running
the spot test is the ladder's minimally destructive rung, reached only when cheaper rungs leave ambiguity
screen classes are one half of the evidence pair the family assignment requires
spot-test class evidence is the usual second agreeing method behind a family assignment
wear windows, color steps, and seams found at examination are the coating map's raw evidence
fraction marks and fineness marks are primary evidence in the solid-clad-plated verdict
the coating map says what any surface reading was actually measuring, which the construction verdict must discount
the pot-metal survival call is the deep-dive the family assignment triggers for its riskiest class
the joint walk works through the physical map the examination built
the non-metal inventory starts from the examination's record of settings and materials
the family sets the porosity prior - die-cast and cast silver are trap-prone where wrought brass is not
assay marks, maker marks, and origin cues are the dating evidence the antique screen runs on
bright white underlayers found in the coating map are the main likely-nickel evidence
the map's signatures are indexed by the family calls that can go wrong
the survival call on pot metal is a direct verdict input for its family
no verdict is issuable while any non-metal element lacks a disposition
the verdict weighs residual identification risk using the map's known miss consequences
only an accepted or conditionally accepted job generates irreversible steps needing consent
the card is the verdict's carrier; without a verdict there is nothing to hand off
sign-offs are attached card content; a card without its authorizations is incomplete at the hard stop
reagent work happens only inside the bench's storage, labeling, PPE, disposal, and segregation obligations
the ladder may only contain method classes the bench can run safely and lawfully as trained
the mandate's no-work-before-verdict rule is enforced physically as the card's incomplete-card hard stop
a transcribed mark becomes a protected feature: any work risking it cannot proceed without a sign-off naming it
an unknown or soft-solder joint caps the available verdict at accept-with-conditions
queue pressure at the verdict desk pushes toward triage on appearance while the ladder demands method time
edges.resolution_rule: identity verification wins for acceptance: no accept verdict without the ladder's evidence pair; refusal on appearance alone is allowed, acceptance is not

edges.why_related: the best hidden spot for a reagent drop is often near settings where a drop can wick into organics or foil
edges.resolution_rule: the organics survey vetoes spot placement; if no safe location exists, escalate to a non-contact instrument class or refer rather than test

edges.why_related: a struck fineness claim and a physical test result can disagree about the same piece
edges.resolution_rule: the verified physical test wins; the mark is flagged counterfeit-suspect or transplanted, and the discrepancy is documented and disclosed

edges.why_related: the customer's identity story and the bench's tested family assignment can contradict each other
edges.resolution_rule: the evidence-pair assignment wins; the claim is corrected with the customer in a documented disclosure conversation before any work proceeds

edges.why_related: the customer's hope for a restored keepsake collides with the honest destruction risk of wet-processing fragile die-cast
edges.resolution_rule: honest risk disclosure and the refusal right dominate: the piece is never risked to keep the job, and the hope is answered with the documented alternatives

edges.why_related: the construction class determines which promises are honest - a worn clad skin cannot be restored to clad by any plate
unverifiable voids and filled bodies drive refusal and referral because trapped chemistry keeps damaging the piece after handover
the zero-cost screens run before any reagent touches the piece - the ladder's nondestructive-first order made physical
each failure traced to a triage miss tightens the specific ladder rung that owned it
a line-side rejection or an under-plate surprise returns the piece to re-examination with the card's query attached
both hunt substrate zones that react with or trap solution, using the same probe-gently-and-document habit

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_identity_verification
conflict_axes.description: The queue rewards fast verdicts while the ladder's evidence-pair rule demands method time on every piece; the pressure is worst on plausible-looking pieces where appearance feels sufficient.
poles: move the queue on experienced appearance calls
hold every acceptance to the two-agreeing-methods rule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: asymmetric gate: refusal may be fast, acceptance never is; batch-verify identical trade lots at lot level to buy back the time

conflict_axes.name: job_revenue_vs_piece_survival
conflict_axes.description: Every refusal costs real revenue and risks the customer relationship, while every marginal acceptance risks a piece the shop may not be able to replace at any price.
poles: accept marginal pieces to keep the book full
refuse or refer whenever survival cannot be honestly bounded
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the mission line decides it: never risk a customer piece to keep a job; price the survivable risk into accept-with-conditions instead of pretending it away

conflict_axes.name: stamped_claim_vs_tested_evidence
conflict_axes.description: Marks and customer stories arrive with social authority the bench's quiet screens lack, and overriding them creates friction the assessor must absorb.
poles: credit the mark and the story
credit only the physical evidence pair
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: marks and stories select which tests to run; they never substitute for them, and every override is documented and disclosed

conflict_axes.name: test_invasiveness_vs_certainty
conflict_axes.description: The decisive tests (spot on exposed core, sacrificial cut) are the ones that mark the piece, while the harmless screens leave honest ambiguity the verdict must then carry.
poles: stay non-destructive and accept undetermined classes
escalate to destructive evidence for a firm answer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: escalate only when the verdict actually turns on the answer, always with documented consent; otherwise record undetermined and handle to the most protective assumption

conflict_axes.name: customer_hope_vs_honest_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: Customers arrive wanting like-new and solid-gold language, and the softer answer closes more jobs today at the price of handover disputes and trade dishonesty.
poles: state the honest capability and wear mechanism before acceptance
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honesty is non-negotiable trade floor: correct solid-gold language, state unachievables at the bench, and let the disclosure record carry the proof it happened

conflict_axes.name: heirloom_value_vs_restoration_desire
conflict_axes.description: The owner of an antique wants it bright again, while patina, original surface, and possible fire gilding are exactly what brightening destroys or endangers.
poles: deliver the shine the owner asked for
protect value and safety by referring the piece out
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: antiques default to refer; any replate of an antique proceeds only after written disclosure of what it erases, and suspected fire-gilt never proceeds at all

conflict_axes.name: stone_masking_vs_removal_vs_refusal
conflict_axes.description: Masking is cheap and keeps the job whole, removal is safe but costly and adds setter risk, and refusal protects the stone at the price of the job.
poles: mask in place and run the piece
remove-and-reset, flag for selective work, or refuse
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: masking is the exception that must be positively justified per element; sentimental weight pushes the call conservative, and the disposition is recorded before the verdict

conflict_axes.name: bench_speed_vs_documentation_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Photographs, transcripts, maps, and named grounds all cost minutes per piece that the bench feels every day, but they are the only assets that decide disputes and train successors.
poles: full baseline record, maps, and named grounds on every customer piece
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale documentation to custody risk: full discipline on customer and heirloom pieces, lot-level records for identical trade batches, never zero

conflict_axes.name: safety_segregation_vs_bench_convenience
conflict_axes.description: The convenient bench keeps reagents at hand and rinses residues to the sink; the safe bench pays the walk to segregated storage and the regulated disposal route every single time.
poles: keep reagents where the work is
hold the storage, segregation, and disposal obligations absolutely
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety obligations are not weighed against convenience - the cyanide-acid segregation line and the no-drain rule are absolute, and layout should make the safe path the short path

edge_cases.description: A white-metal piece pulls faintly on the magnet and gets booked as stainless when it is nickel-plated brass
edge_cases.trigger: a single-cue magnet reading taken as a verdict on a plated piece
edge_cases.mitigation: treat faint pulls as a nickel-layer warning class; require a second agreeing method before any family entry, and record the contradiction as an escalation

edge_cases.description: A piece stamped 925 fails the silver test on a hidden point
edge_cases.trigger: a counterfeit or transplanted fineness mark contradicted by chemistry
edge_cases.mitigation: the test wins; flag the mark counterfeit-suspect, document the discrepancy, and disclose it to the customer before deciding the verdict

edge_cases.description: Gold-filled stock and heavy vintage plate present identically to every surface method available at the bench
edge_cases.trigger: a construction call on which the job plan turns cannot be settled non-destructively
edge_cases.mitigation: record the class as undetermined, handle to the most protective assumption, and offer a consented sacrificial cut only if the verdict genuinely turns on it

edge_cases.description: A spot test on an old plated piece reads the coating and the assessor books the core as that metal
edge_cases.trigger: surface chemistry mistaken for core identity on coated goods
edge_cases.mitigation: the coating map is consulted before any test is interpreted; core claims require a consented core-exposing point or stay unknown

edge_cases.description: A pearl glued into a cup mount is discovered only after the piece was accepted
edge_cases.trigger: a closed or tight setting hiding an organic element from the inventory
edge_cases.mitigation: the discovery voids the accept verdict automatically; the piece returns to triage and the customer is contacted before any further step

edge_cases.description: A gilt bronze clock case arrives for brightening and is plausibly fire-gilt ormolu
edge_cases.trigger: an antique gilt-bronze object class with pre-industrial age cues
edge_cases.mitigation: hard refer to a conservator with the reasoning documented; no torch, strip, or ultrasonic contact in-shop under any customer instruction

edge_cases.description: A hollow bangle soldered shut gives no way to verify whether its void is dry or already contaminated
edge_cases.trigger: an unverifiable internal void in a piece proposed for immersion
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse immersion routes for unverifiable voids; offer referral or a dry-route alternative flag and record the trap as the named ground

edge_cases.description: A gray seam at a repaired clasp reveals soft solder only after old plate is worn through at the joint
edge_cases.trigger: a prior repair with unknown low-temperature solder hidden under coating
edge_cases.mitigation: any repair joint of unknown solder inherits the worst-assumption class; the verdict caps at accept-with-conditions with the joint photographed and disclaimed

edge_cases.description: A customer refuses stone removal but insists the set piece go through the tanks anyway
edge_cases.trigger: a customer instruction that contradicts the organics disposition
edge_cases.mitigation: customer instruction cannot override piece-survival triage; the shop offers removal-and-reset, a selective-process flag, or declines, and documents the offered alternatives

edge_cases.description: A brooch combines a silver body with a steel pin and spring, so no single family entry fits the assembly
edge_cases.trigger: a mixed-substrate assembly where components need different downstream handling
edge_cases.mitigation: record each component's family separately; flag disassembly need or refer, and note the spring as an embrittlement-caution class for any line decision

edge_cases.description: A weighted candlestick or filled knife handle would breach its fill in any heated or immersed step
edge_cases.trigger: filled construction detected by weight anomaly and seam evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: classify as filled construction, exclude immersion and heat routes, disclose why the wanted service is unavailable, and refer where a dry alternative exists

edge_cases.description: A customer calls mid-job asking to also buff out deep scratches, which would breach remaining plate near a hallmark
edge_cases.trigger: scope creep after the original sign-off was given
edge_cases.mitigation: the original signature does not cover the new step; the piece returns to the sign-off gate and the route card is re-issued before any added irreversible work

workflow.action: Post and enforce the triage mandate
workflow.description: Fix the no-work-before-verdict rule, the four verdict classes, and the assessor's refusal authority
workflow.artifact: posted triage policy with named verdict classes
workflow.gate: no route into wheel, ultrasonic, or tank exists that bypasses a recorded verdict

workflow.action: Interview the customer and capture claims
workflow.description: Record provenance, prior work, skin-contact use, service goal, and heirloom weight as claims to verify
workflow.gate: claims are separated from observations and the service goal is stated

workflow.action: Examine and photograph the piece before first touch
workflow.description: Build the baseline condition record and the physical map of joints, stones, hollows, and marks
workflow.artifact: dated condition photographs plus written condition note
workflow.gate: photographs exist before any test result appears in the file

workflow.description: Magnet classes and weight-for-bulk feel, read as classes with contradictions flagged
workflow.gate: every screen entry carries cue, reading, class interpretation, and any escalation note

workflow.action: Find, transcribe, and interpret every mark
workflow.description: Fineness, plated-goods, fraction, maker, and origin marks read as claims that steer testing
workflow.artifact: mark transcript with locations and class interpretations
workflow.gate: each mark is tagged verify-pending until a physical test agrees

workflow.action: Spot test where the ladder still leaves ambiguity
workflow.description: Commercial kit per instructions on an organics-cleared hidden point, with consent where visible or core-exposing
workflow.artifact: spot-test record with product, location, and reading
workflow.gate: the organics-cleared note and any required consent are attached to every test entry

workflow.action: Assign the substrate family with its evidence pair
workflow.description: Family assignment on two agreeing method classes, or unknown-held, with the downstream fork named
workflow.artifact: family entry with evidence pair and fork flag
workflow.gate: no family entry rests on a single method or a guess

workflow.action: Map coatings and decide the construction class
workflow.description: Coating map from wear windows and swabs, then the solid-clad-plated verdict with stated confidence
workflow.gate: surface readings are interpreted against the coating map and undetermined classes carry the protective-assumption note

workflow.description: Joint map, non-metal inventory with dispositions, trap zones, antique and fire-gilt screen, nickel flag
workflow.artifact: risk-zone map covering joints, organics, traps, antique status, and nickel status
workflow.gate: every risk class is explicitly cleared or flagged - none left blank

workflow.action: Deliver the verdict with named grounds
workflow.description: Integrate all surveys into accept, accept-with-conditions, refuse, or refer, citing evidence
workflow.gate: the verdict cites the family evidence and every relevant survey output; refusals and referrals carry their reasons

workflow.action: Disclose honestly and obtain irreversibility sign-off
workflow.description: State capability, wear mechanism, and unachievables; obtain specific written consent per irreversible step
workflow.gate: every irreversible step maps to a signature naming that step and its risk

workflow.action: Issue the route card and hand off
workflow.description: Compile facts, flags, verdict, conditions, and sign-offs into the traveler the downstream benches consume
workflow.artifact: complete route card accompanying the piece
workflow.gate: no empty fields; unknowns written as unknown-held; the line may refuse an incomplete card

priority_rationale: The mandate and bench-safety frame come first because they define when work may happen at all; interview and examination build the claims and baseline every test needs; the ladder and its screens verify identity before the family, coating, and construction calls that everything forks on; the risk-zone surveys must finish before any verdict; and the verdict, disclosure, sign-off, and route card come last because they integrate and carry everything upstream into the one artifact the rest of the shop consumes.

dominance_rules.rule: Piece survival beats job revenue wherever they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: a lost fee is recoverable, a customer's irreplaceable piece is not, and the shop's name follows the piece
dominance_rules.trigger: a marginal piece could be accepted only by discounting a survival risk
dominance_rules.action: refuse or refer with documented grounds, or accept only with the risk named, priced, and signed

dominance_rules.rule: Verified test evidence beats stamped marks and customer claims
dominance_rules.rationale: marks and stories are claims by others; the bench's evidence pair is the only thing the shop itself verified
dominance_rules.trigger: a mark or customer statement contradicts the tested family or construction class
dominance_rules.action: book the tested result, flag the mark or claim, and disclose the discrepancy before proceeding

dominance_rules.rule: The organics default beats process convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: stones, pearls, and organics are the least reversible losses the bench can cause
dominance_rules.trigger: a set or organic-bearing piece is proposed for any wet or heated route
dominance_rules.action: hold the no-tank default: remove-and-reset, positively justified masking, a selective-process flag, or refuse

dominance_rules.rationale: verbal consent evaporates exactly when it is needed, in the dispute after the irreversible step
dominance_rules.trigger: any irreversible step is about to proceed on spoken agreement
dominance_rules.action: stop; obtain the specific written authorization or do not perform the step

dominance_rules.rule: Safety segregation beats bench convenience absolutely
dominance_rules.rationale: the cyanide-acid line and the disposal rules are life-safety and legal obligations, not preferences
dominance_rules.trigger: reagent storage, use, or disposal is about to deviate from the obligation classes
dominance_rules.action: block the shortcut; restore segregated storage, labeled containers, and the regulated disposal route before testing resumes

dominance_rules.rationale: most verdicts do not turn on the answer a destructive test would give, and the mark it leaves is permanent
dominance_rules.trigger: a destructive rung is proposed while cheaper rungs remain unrun or the verdict does not turn on the result
dominance_rules.action: run the cheaper rungs or record undetermined with protective handling; escalate only with consent and necessity

dominance_rules.rule: Refer beats improvise outside the bench's competence
dominance_rules.rationale: antiques, fire-gilt, valuable stones, and assay-grade questions have specialists whose absence the bench cannot fake
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece's screen result lands in conservator, setter, or assay-class territory
dominance_rules.action: refer with documented reasoning instead of attempting the work in-shop

dominance_rules.rationale: representing plated goods as solid or promising wear-years is the trade dishonesty the whole program forbids
dominance_rules.trigger: optimistic framing would close the job faster than the honest capability statement
dominance_rules.action: state the coating status, the wear mechanism, and any unachievable outcome before acceptance, and record it

dominance_rules.rationale: an incomplete card exports triage's unfinished work to benches that cannot do it
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece is ready to move with card fields empty or guessed
